tools.name: next_action
tools.description: The single next action of the project (the same as `next --json`): the action, the stage card, whether a person must act (`human`), and what to say.

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: The budgeted context pack of one task: everything it needs, with what was left out. Use this instead of reading the repository.

tools.name: claim_task
tools.description: Claim a task with a lease and its file paths, so other agents cannot take overlapping paths. Fails with CLAIM_CONFLICT (holder and paths) when another live claim overlaps.

tools.name: release_task
tools.description: Release a claim you hold. Marking the task done releases it too.

tools.name: task_start
tools.description: Start a task (the same gates as `task <ID> start`). If the task is claimed, only the holder may start it.

tools.name: task_done
tools.description: Mark a task done with a hand-off note (the same gates as `task <ID> done`: tests first, commit, allowed paths, quick checks).

tools.name: run_verify
tools.description: Run the checks of a change and write evidence. `quick` runs only the fast checks (`check --quick`); otherwise the full `verify`, which judges every typed acceptance line and writes evidence with a fingerprint.

tools.name: record_evidence
tools.description: Record a check that ran outside the engine (for example a test run you did) as evidence. A pass recorded here is a check, never a person's look.

tools.name: advance
tools.description: Move a change to the next status through its gates. Returns the new status, or GATE_REFUSED with `missing` saying what to do first.

tools.name: status
tools.description: The project status: features, changes, next actions, issues (the same as `status --json`).

tools.name: show
tools.description: One record with its fields, links, slices, changes and backlinks (the same as `show <ID> --json`).

tools.name: trace
tools.description: Follow a feature or requirement: slices, changes, tasks, tests, evidence and code (the same as `trace <ID> --json`).

tools.name: new_record
tools.description: Create a record (source, question, assumption, outcome, requirement, nfr, concept, invariant, workflow, decision, contract, component, rule, test, release, flag, experiment) and return its ID.

tools.name: request_approval
tools.description: Ask a person to approve or look. It only creates a request in the log; it never approves anything. A person answers in a terminal or with a signed token.
